$comment: The tool surface, as JSON Schema, registered verbatim: src/tools.ts hands these to fromJsonSchema, so what a client sees is this file. Branch requirements ('task needs key') are stated in the discriminator's description and enforced in the handler, which can say what was missing -- not in allOf/if/then, which cost 566 bytes of every conversation to restate it less helpfully. `reset` stays its own tool because hosts grant permission per tool NAME. There is no delete_graph: reset empties a graph, and an empty graph is not listed, so emptying IS deleting.

what.description: board: counts + ready queue, and draws the card. ready: startable tasks only. task: one task whole — detail, dependencies, what blocks it (needs `key`). graphs: every graph on this connector. mermaid: a diagram — narrow it with keys/depth/direction/status, it is the one answer that costs real tokens.

graph.description: Graph handle from an earlier result. Omit for the most recent.

limit.description: How many ready tasks to name; the rest are counted.

keys.description: Draw only around these tasks. Omit for the whole graph; keys that match nothing draw nothing.

status.description: Keep only these statuses. Seeds survive regardless.

max_chars.description: The diagram budget, default 4000. Raise or lower it freely; the default exists so a big graph cannot land whole by accident, not to stop you asking.

override_token.description: From a previous overflow: renders that graph whole without needing to know its size. Single use.

op.description: plan: add or change tasks and dependencies — MERGES, never deletes, so a new plan needs no wipe (send `tasks`, `edges` or `title`). update: one task’s status or fields (needs `key`). unlink: remove dependency edges, keeping the tasks (needs `edges`). Emptying or deleting a whole graph is `reset`, not here.

graph.description: Graph handle. Omit for the most recent; op=plan mints one when there is none.

new_graph.description: Start a separate graph instead of merging. Ignored when `graph` is given.

title.description: Names the GRAPH (op=plan). Renaming a task is `task_title`.

tasks.description: Tasks to create or update, matched by key.

key.description: Required, and must mean something: a slug from the title, e.g. "write-tests". "T3" and bare numbers are refused.

title.description: Short imperative title. Kept whole; shortened to 80 chars where it repeats.

detail.description: Be generous: retrievable via read(what=task) and the graph resource, but left out of the receipts every other call returns, so length costs nothing per call.

status.description: Omitted leaves an existing task's status alone.

priority.description: Higher sorts first in the ready queue. Default 0.

edges.description: op=plan adds these, op=unlink removes them. { from, to } reads "from depends on to": to must be done first. Cycles and self-edges are refused; duplicates are ignored.

status.description: Start, finish, reopen or cancel a task. Reopening does not reopen its dependents.

task_title.description: Renames the task. Separate from `title`, which renames the graph.

tools.name: reset
tools.title: Reset graph
tools.description: Irreversible. Empties a graph: every task and dependency in it. An emptied graph stops being listed, so this is also how a graph is deleted; the handle keeps working if you write to it again. Only when the user says clear, wipe, start over or delete. Never to make room for a new plan — write(op=plan) merges.

graph.description: Which graph. Required: this is the one call with no defaulting to the most recent.
